newsitem.title: USA: Apple's Scalise to head semiconductor group.
newsitem.headline: Apple's Scalise to head semiconductor group.

text.p: The Semiconductor Industry Association's board of directors said on Tuesday it selected Apple Computer Inc. Executive Vice President of Operations George Scalise to be the SIA's new president.
Scalise, 63, is due to join the SIA on June 2 and succeeds Thomas Armstrong, who left the nationwide trade association in March, the SIA said in a statement.
Scalise and Apple officials were not immediately available to comment on the appointment.
Scalise, who joined Apple last spring to help the company's then freshly-appointed CEO Gil Amelio turn around the struggling computer maker, has a long history in the semiconductor industry.

Before joining Apple Computer, he was executive vice president and chief administration officer for National Semiconductor Corp., based in Santa Clara, Calif., where he had been working on Amelio's turnaround team.
He has also served as a senior executive at Maxtor, Advanced Micro Devices, Fairchild Semiconductor and Motorola Inc.

Scalise has worked on the SIA's public policy comittee and served as chairman of that group, as a director of the Semiconductor Research Corporation and, from 1993 to 1996, with the SEMATECH semiconductor industry group.
